subject: MSA / Order Form — SLA credit structure & maintenance window negotiation
messages:
From: Amy Lee <amy@starlitehealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@starlitehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Aug 2025 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood MSA/Order Form — proposed SLA redlines

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the draft MSA and the order form — Starlite's procurement and engineering teams reviewed the SLA section and attached a short list of redlines (attached: Starlite_SLA_Redlines_v1.pdf). The high-level asks are: 99.95% uptime (monthly), a graduated service-credit table starting at a 30-minute major outage threshold, and a commitment to 1-hour P1 acknowledgement / 4-hour P1 mitigation windows.

We also need tighter controls around maintenance windows: we prefer monthly windows not to exceed 2 hours and advance notice of at least 72 hours for any non-emergency maintenance. Finally, we'd like logging/audit evidence for uptime calculations (tenancy-level telemetry) to be included as part of periodic reporting.

Can you confirm Redwood's position on those three items and share an initial redline or counterproposal by EOD Thursday? If helpful, Tom Saunders (Starlite's outside counsel) will be looped in — copying procurement above.

Appreciate it,

Amy Lee
Head of Procurement
Starlite Health
amy@starlitehealth.com
(415) 555-0142
Attachment: Starlite_SLA_Redlines_v1.pdf (PDF, 34KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Amy Lee <amy@starlitehealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Aug 2025 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood MSA/Order Form — proposed SLA redlines

Amy — thanks for the clear list and the PDF. We're glad Starlite is prioritizing availability and observability. Quick read-through and high-level responses below; I'll get my team to provide a redline doc, but I wanted to align on expectations first.

Short answers:
- Uptime: Redwood's standard hosted offering commits to 99.9% by default; we can discuss 99.95 for this engagement but need to confirm the scope (global vs single-region).
- Service credits: we can support a graduated credit table; need to cap total credits to mitigate unbounded exposure (we usually cap at 12 months' fees for a single incident or X% of monthly spend).
- P1 response: we can commit to 1-hour acknowledgement. Mitigation/restore timelines depend on incident class — we can commit to initial mitigation within 4 hours and continuous updates thereafter for P1s.
- Maintenance: we typically schedule regular monthly maintenance windows (up to 3 hours for major infra work) with 72-hour notice; if Starlite needs a hard 2-hour cap, ops will need to confirm feasibility for certain infrastructure changes.

Looped in Neha for legal redlines and Laura for ops feasibility. Neha/Laura — can you review Starlite's PDF and propose counter-language? Amy — can you confirm whether the 99.95 request applies to the Account region only or to all traffic globally?

Proposed next step: 30-min call Thursday morning to walk through the redlines and land on a short list for legal? I can host — propose Thu 08/14 09:00 PT.

Thanks,

Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Attachment: (none)

From: Amy Lee <amy@starlitehealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@starlitehealth.com>, Tom Saunders <tsaunders@cooley.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Aug 2025 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood MSA/Order Form — proposed SLA redlines

Karthik — thanks for the quick reply and for looping in Neha and Laura.

We view uptime as account-level (all traffic in the primary region where our workload will run). 99.95% is preferred; Starlite is sensitive to availability impact on critical patient workflows. The credit cap we are comfortable with is 6 months' average monthly fees, not the 12-month cap you mentioned.

Tom is on copy to help with precise redline language; he's our counsel and will push back on language that ties credits to a narrow metric (we want credits tied to customer-observed downtime rather than internal platform health counters).

We can do Thu 08/14 09:00 PT for the call. Please send calendar invite. Also attached a draft maintenance-calendar.xlsx showing preferred blackout/change freeze windows for our clinical hours.

Amy
Attachment: maintenance-calendar.xlsx (XLSX, 12KB)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Aug 2025 14:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood MSA/Order Form — proposed SLA redlines

Amy / Karthik — I reviewed Starlite_SLA_Redlines_v1.pdf and drafted an internal redline set; attaching the tracked changes (Redlined_MSA_OrderForm.docx). High-level summary of our position below — please note these are proposed company positions and we should confirm on the call.

Key points:
1) Uptime definition: propose to define "Service Availability" using successful request rate measured at the service egress per customer tenancy during the billing period, with an explicit list of excluded events (force majeure, third-party provider failures, customer misconfiguration, DDoS not routed through our mitigation layer).
2) Measurement & evidence: willing to provide monthly uptime reports and 30 days of telemetry logs upon request; we prefer logs to be redacted for multi-tenant correlation IDs.
3) Credit table: propose a graduated credit table but with a 6-month fee cap (we can be flexible on the cap but prefer commercial threshold tied to customer's ARR band). Example: <99.0% = 50% of monthly fee, 99.0–99.5% = 20%, 99.5–99.9% = 10%.
4) P1 definition & response: accept 1-hour initial acknowledgement. For restoration time, we will commit to continuous mitigation and updates; we avoid hard restore SLAs because they can be impacted by mitigation complexity and third-party dependencies.
5) Maintenance windows: propose monthly maintenance window up to 3 hours with 72-hour notice for non-emergency, and emergency maintenance allowed with notice as soon as practicable. For customers requiring a strict 2-hour cap, we can offer a dedicated capacity SKU (with higher cost) or contractual carveouts limiting major infra changes.

Ops (Laura), please confirm whether the dedicated capacity option or tighter window commitments are operationally feasible for a Starlite-sized deployment. Amy — Tom, I included some alternate wording that ties credits to customer-observed error rates rather than internal counters; please review and flag problematic language.

Thanks,

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Attachment: Redlined_MSA_OrderForm.docx (DOCX, 48KB)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 14 Aug 2025 16:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood MSA/Order Form — proposed SLA redlines

Amy / Neha / Karthik — ops read-through and feasibility notes below ahead of our call tomorrow morning.

1) 99.95% vs 99.9%: Technically feasible in a single-region deployment for the core inference service, but it materially constrains maintenance and rolling upgrade strategies. 99.95% reduces our ability to perform larger kernel/driver or CUDA-level updates without rolling restarts impacting tail latencies. If Starlite requires 99.95% account-level, recommend: (a) define the metric precisely (successful request completion within X seconds), and (b) accept limited maintenance exclusions + option for Dedicated Capacity (reserved GPU pool) for a higher fee.

2) Credit structure: We can implement the 3-tier credit table Neha suggested but ask that credits be tied to the platform-level metric we provide (per-tenancy request success rate). Tying to customer-observed downtime is ambiguous unless Starlite agrees on a measurement endpoint (we can expose a healthcheck/edge metric).

3) Maintenance windows: We can commit to regular monthly maintenance windows of up to 2 hours for Starlite if they accept the Dedicated Capacity SKU. For hosted standard tenants, keep the 3-hour window and 72-hour notice. Emergency maintenance will be allowed with as much notice as possible.

4) Monitoring & evidence: We will provide monthly availability reports and 90 days of telemetry; for audit requests we can provide redacted logs under an NDA if needed.

Next steps:
- Karthik to send calendar invite for Thu 08/14 09:00 PT (confirmed).
- Neha to circulate the redlined doc in final form post-call.
- If Starlite prefers 99.95% without Dedicated Capacity, we will need to price that as an SLA premium and define clear carveouts.

Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Operations, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
Attachment: (none)
